flashcard_questions.q: What does it mean to call memory volatile?
flashcard_questions.a: It loses all of its contents when the power is switched off.

flashcard_questions.q: What does non-volatile mean when describing memory?
flashcard_questions.a: It keeps its contents even when the power is switched off.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of primary storage is volatile and can be both read and written?
What does RAM store while a computer is running?
flashcard_questions.a: The programs and data the computer is using at that moment.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of primary storage is non-volatile and normally read only?
What is the bootstrap program stored in ROM?
flashcard_questions.a: A small program that runs at switch-on and begins loading the operating system.

flashcard_questions.q: Why are the start-up instructions kept in ROM rather than in RAM?
flashcard_questions.a: ROM is non-volatile, so the instructions are still there after the power has been off.

flashcard_questions.q: Why must a program be copied into primary storage before it runs?
flashcard_questions.a: The CPU can only read directly from primary storage.

flashcard_questions.q: Which is usually larger in a computer, RAM or ROM?
flashcard_questions.a: RAM, because it must hold everything currently in use.

flashcard_questions.q: What is virtual memory on a computer?
flashcard_questions.a: An area of secondary storage used as if it were extra RAM.

flashcard_questions.q: When does a computer start using virtual memory?
What is moved out of RAM into virtual memory?
flashcard_questions.a: Data that is not being used at that moment.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does heavy use of virtual memory slow a computer down?
flashcard_questions.a: Secondary storage is far slower than RAM, so the CPU waits while data is swapped.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the best fix for a computer relying on virtual memory?
